newsitem.title: USA: Montana Power files transition plan.
newsitem.headline: Montana Power files transition plan.

text.p: Montana Power Co said Tuesday it filed with the Montana Public Service Commission a transition plan in line with recent state legislation to restructure Montana's electric utility industry.

"We believe the plan we are filing today meets all of the new law's requirements and provides a schedule to implement competition for all customers as soon as it's administratively feasible," Perry Cole, vice president of business development and regulatory affairs at the utility, said in a statement.
The Montana law calls for choice of energy supplier to be available on July 1, 1998 to the 75 to 100 largest users of electricity, with all consumers able to choose their supplier by July 1, 2002.
Montana Power's plan also anticipates a transition to choicethat would give as many as 10 percent of residential and business customers choice by July 2000.
As many as half of Montana Power's customers would have choice by July 1, 2001, and all customers would have a selected electricity supplier by July 1, 2002.
The plan also proposes pilot programs beginning July 1, 1998, to test and improve administrative functions related to restructuring.
The state commission is scheduled to begin public hearings on the process next February.
